resources.string: Folders of this type cannot be moved: a Send only folder never receives files from the other devices, so it would stay empty in the new directory. To move it, change its type to Send and receive, move it, then change it back.
The other devices have items this phone lacks; overriding would delete them there. Open the folder again to see how many.
Sync is running but does not respond.
File versions and synced folders cannot share a directory: versions inside a synced folder are synced to every device.
The sync service answered with HTTP %1$d.
device id, identity, certificate, key, cert.pem, key.pem, import
sync, syncthing, folder, device, keepass, wi-fi only, charging, encrypted, untrusted, ignore patterns, versions
discovery, relay, nat, bandwidth, rate limit
Another device shares this folder. Choose where it is kept on this phone and how it syncs.
Enter the device ID shown on the other device (in its sync app\'s device identity).
Enter the device ID shown on the other device, or scan its QR code.
A new folder synced with the devices chosen below. They are asked to accept it.

One address per line. dynamic: found through discovery, by the global discovery servers from any network while global discovery is on, and by local discovery on the same network. Fixed: tcp://host:port or quic://host:port (port 22000 when left out), or relay://host:port/?id=… through a relay server.

A fixed address that does not answer, such as a home LAN address while the phone is elsewhere, is tried again every %1$d s (Retry interval, under Discovery and connections); each try wakes the mobile radio and uses battery.

A fixed address that does not answer, such as a home LAN address while the phone is elsewhere, is tried again at the Retry interval under Discovery and connections; each try wakes the mobile radio and uses battery.
Keeping it connects at once on that network; with dynamic alone and local discovery on, the device is still found there, without tries elsewhere.
Folders this device shares are added in the sync storage without asking
Sync stops while no charger is connected
When a file changed on two devices at once, the other version is kept next to it with .sync-conflict- in its name. Keep the right version and delete the copy on any device; the deletion is synced.
Pausing a device stops syncing with it until it is resumed.
A device ID has letters and digits only
A device ID has 52 or 56 characters without dashes
Other devices show this name for this phone.
Use letters A to Z, digits, space, dot, dash and underscore; do not start with a dot
A directory in the sync storage, created when the folder is added. Letters A to Z, digits, space, dot, dash and underscore.
The public discovery servers, IPv4 only
The public discovery servers, IPv6 only

One server per line. default: the public discovery servers (default-v4 or default-v6: one address family only). A server of your own (stdiscosrv): https://host:port/?id=<its device ID>; add &noannounce to only look devices up there, or &nolookup to only announce this phone. Plain http:// only with id (or insecure) and noannounce.
Not used while global discovery is off
Every device gets the files unencrypted

%1$s gets %2$s encrypted with this password and cannot read the files. Every trusted device that shares the folder with it must use the same password. The password stays in the sync service; it is never shown again.
%1$s gets %2$s unencrypted from now on and can read every file. If it is an untrusted device, Syncthing stops sharing the folder with it instead.
Pausing a folder stops its sync on this phone only.
Every device syncing the folder uses the same ID.
A folder with this ID exists
Sync keeps folders the same on this phone and the other devices, directly between them. Folders are kept in the sync storage of this phone, which only the sync service and Lujarch can read.
Find devices anywhere through the discovery servers below
Incomplete backup; it cannot be restored
Folders of the imported configuration are kept in:
Backups stay in the sync storage of this device, readable only by the sync service.
Sync creates a new certificate and private key when it starts.

Sync creates a new certificate and private key when it starts. Other devices know this phone by its current device ID and will not connect until the new one is added on them. The current identity is kept as a backup.
A new certificate and key; other devices must add the new device ID
Certificate and private key, optionally with a configuration
The device identity (a certificate and its private key) is how the other devices recognize this phone. When it is replaced, the previous identity is kept as a backup.
Keep this device\'s devices and folders
Off: the new identity starts without devices or folders
Not set up. Import an identity or create one.
Set up; the device ID is shown while sync runs
The identity saved on %1$s replaces the current one, which is kept as a backup.
A new identity is waiting to be installed
%1$s can no longer ask to connect. This can be undone in Ignored devices.
An ignored device cannot ask to connect. Tap it to let it ask again.
The patterns are kept in the folder on this phone and are not sent to other devices. #include reads only files inside the folder.
One pattern per line, as in Syncthing\'s .stignore: /name for the top level only, ! to keep something again, (?d) to allow deleting, // for comments.
No patterns: every file is synced
Files and folders that are not synced (.stignore)
A line is longer than %1$d characters
The files are checked and installed when sync starts.
The imported identity replaces the current one, which is kept as a backup. Other devices must know the imported device ID.

The files are read only for this import, checked by the Lujarch system service and installed with the sync service as their owner. The private key is not kept anywhere else. Folders of an imported configuration are placed in the sync storage.
Choose the certificate (cert.pem) and private key (key.pem) of another device or of a backup. A configuration (config.xml) brings its devices and folders along.
Add the devices this device shares folders with, and share those folders with them
Default: TCP and QUIC on port 22000

One address per line: tcp://0.0.0.0:22000 or quic://0.0.0.0:22000 (0.0.0.0 or no host: every network; port 0: any free port). default: TCP and QUIC on port 22000. Other devices connect to this phone at these ports when they have its address or find it through discovery. Leave empty and this phone only connects to others.
None: this phone only connects to others
Find devices on the same local network

Synced folders are kept in the sync storage of this phone, which only the sync service and Lujarch can read; other apps and shared storage (Download, DCIM) cannot reach it. Each folder is one directory there.

%1$s moves to %2$s. It is added again there with the same ID and settings and starts from an empty index: its files come from the other devices, or are taken over when they are already in that directory. %3$s keeps its files. Files that differ from the other devices\' versions are kept as conflict copies.
Ask the router to open a port (UPnP, NAT-PMP)
These settings apply to every device. A device with fixed addresses is reached at them whatever the discovery settings.
Discovery servers, listen addresses, relays, NAT traversal, retries and rate limits
Set up a device identity to start syncing
Enter a whole number in range
Overriding would delete files on the other devices that this phone does not have.
Stop syncing with every device until resumed

This device wants to sync with this phone.

Device ID: %1$s
Address: %2$s

Add it to sync with it; ignore it to stop further requests; later keeps the request until it asks again.
This folder is shared encrypted: this phone keeps the encrypted data (receive encrypted) and cannot open its files.
%1$s shares this folder (ID %2$s).\n\nAdd it to choose where it is kept on this phone; ignore it to stop further offers of this folder.
That device keeps this folder encrypted: adding it needs an encryption password for the device.

Seconds between tries to reach a device that is not connected, at each of its addresses (5 to 86400). A longer interval wakes the mobile radio less often while a device cannot be reached (for example a home LAN address while the phone is elsewhere); the device then connects up to that much later once it can be reached.

One per line. A relay server of your own (strelaysrv): relay://host:22067/?id=<its device ID>, with &token=… when it requires one. A relay pool: dynamic+https://host/path. default: the public pool (dynamic+https://relays.syncthing.net/endpoint). Used only while Relays is on; the data stays encrypted end to end.
Not used while relays are off
Connect through relays when a direct connection fails; the data stays encrypted
This phone stops syncing with %1$s. Shared folders and their files stay.
%1$s stops syncing on this phone. Its files stay in %2$s, and other devices keep their copies.
Add a device that takes over its folders and settings, such as a new cloud server, then remove or pause this one
Enter the device ID of the device that takes over from %1$s.
Enter the device ID of the device that takes over from %1$s, or scan its QR code.
%1$s gets the settings of %2$s and its folders the same way (encrypted with the same password where %2$s gets them encrypted): %3$s.
%1$s gets the settings of %2$s. %2$s shares no folder.
Enter the ID of a different device: this one belongs to the device being replaced or to this phone.
Then pause %1$s (resume it to switch back)
Permissions are wrong: the vault and identity changes may fail
Keeps another device\'s encrypted data without being able to read it; set when an encrypted folder is added and not changeable
Changes from other devices are applied here; changes on this phone are not sent
Changes on this phone are sent; changes on other devices are not applied here
Changes on any device are synced to all
%1$s gets every folder encrypted from now on. Set an encryption password for it on each folder\'s page before sharing a folder with it.
%1$s gets every folder encrypted from now on. Syncthing stops sharing these folders with it until they have an encryption password for it: %2$s.
Every folder shared with it is encrypted with a password; it cannot read the files

Versions are kept on this phone only and are not synced. External versioning is not offered: it runs a command from the sync configuration, which would let a changed configuration run programs as the sync service.
Files replaced or deleted by other devices are not kept
A relative path without . or .. parts
A path under .stversions, such as .stversions/phone. Any other place in the folder is synced like its files, so the versions would reach the other devices.
A directory of the sync storage
This place is synced with the folder: the versions would be sent to the other devices. Use a path under .stversions or a directory of the sync storage.
A fixed number of versions of each file is kept
Versions are thinned out with age: one per hour for a day, one per day for a month, one per week after that
The last version of each replaced or deleted file is kept
Sync starts when its run conditions are met
Waiting for Wi-Fi and a charger
Notice changes on this phone as they happen
Sync stops while no Wi-Fi network is connected (a Wi-Fi network without internet counts)
Sync uses it as soon as its conditions are met.
Sync uses it when it is turned on.
